title: How to edit an STL file and make it parametric
heading: How to edit an STL file with AI and make it parametric
description: An STL or 3MF is only a mesh of triangles. Let SOMA AI rebuild a downloaded part as a parametric model, change it in plain words and export it for printing.
summary: A downloaded desk organizer, rebuilt by SOMA AI as a parametric model, changed to fit business cards and a third drawer, and exported for the slicer.

video.title: Turn a Downloaded STL or 3MF into an Editable CAD Model with AI (Free & Open Source)

chapters.label: SOMA AI rebuilds it as a parametric model
Make the drawers fit business cards
A third drawer, sketched with Mark up
Compare with the original and export

answer: An STL or 3MF file is only a mesh of flat triangles, so there is no width or wall thickness you could simply change. Instead of pushing triangles around, import the file into SOMA and ask SOMA AI to rebuild it as a parametric model, with the original as a see-through reference; then change sizes with sliders or in plain words and export a new 3MF or STL. The rebuild is a new model made by the AI, so compare it with the original and check the measurements that matter before you print.
need: SOMA, free and open source, for Windows, macOS or Linux.

A sign-in for SOMA AI: a ChatGPT Plus or Pro plan, or an API key from Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI, Google Gemini, OpenRouter or OpenCode. SOMA is free, the AI runs on your plan or key. The cheapest way to start is an OpenCode Go subscription for about $10 a month. In the video SOMA AI runs on GPT-6.1 Sol with high effort.
The STL or 3MF file, and a license that allows changes. The desk organizer in the video is under CC BY-SA 4.0.
The measurements of what must fit, here a business card: 85 by 55 mm.
A 3D printer and its slicer to print the result.

steps.title: Find a part and check its license
text: The part in the video is a desk organizer by GummieGecko8477 on Printables: two drawers in front, a deep cup for pens at the back. The goal is to keep business cards in the drawers and to add one more drawer.

Check the license before you change a part. This one is Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike: you may change it, as long as you credit the author and share your version under the same license. Then download the file. Here it is a 3MF, the format slicers use; an STL works just the same.

steps.title: Import the file and look at it
text: In SOMA, start a new model, click Import at the top and pick the downloaded file. It goes into the inputs folder, where SOMA AI can use it.

Click the file, and SOMA shows it in the viewer: the body and the two drawers, laid out the way they are printed. Switch on the wireframe and you see what the file really is: a mesh of flat triangles, with no width to change and no wall thickness, just corner points.
The drawers are also small: inside, they are 58 by 57 mm. A business card is 85 by 55 mm, so it will not go in.

image.alt: The downloaded Organizer.3mf in SOMA as a wireframe of triangles: the body and two drawers laid out for printing, with the banner Viewing inputs/Organizer.3mf, view only, and a Back to model button

steps.title: Ask SOMA AI to rebuild it
text: Click the SOMA AI tab. In the video the model is GPT-6.1 Sol with the effort set to High, so it thinks things through. Then say what you want in plain words: rebuild the organizer as a parametric model, with the drawers in place, and keep the original as a see-through reference.

SOMA AI opens the file, finds the three parts and measures the walls, the slots and the drawers. Then it builds them as a real model and checks that the drawers slide out freely. In the video this took 7 min 41 s, shown sped up.

The result is the body and the two drawers at the original size of 65 by 125 by 95 mm. The structure tree lists the new parts, and the original ones as references. The original sits in the same place, see-through: hide it and show it again with the eye in the structure tree to compare.
steps.prompt: inputs/Organizer.3mf is a desk organizer I downloaded: a body and two drawers, laid out for printing. Rebuild it as a parametric model with the same shapes and sizes, standing upright on the desk with the drawers in their slots. Show the original parts as a see-through reference in the same places. Make the important sizes parameters, like the width, the depth and the drawer height.

image.alt: The rebuilt desk organizer as a solid blue model with two drawers; the structure tree lists Body, Lower drawer and Upper drawer, and below References the original body and drawers, the original body hidden; SOMA AI's chat on the right says it worked for 7 min 41 s

steps.title: Change sizes with Parameters
text: In the Parameters tab are the sizes SOMA AI made adjustable: here the overall width and depth, the drawer height, the drawer wall thickness and two clearances.
Drag a slider, and the model rebuilds within seconds, without SOMA AI. Change the width or the drawer height, and the drawers and their slots change together. Reset all brings the sizes back.

image.alt: The Parameters panel with the drawer height slider set to 29 mm, range 18 to 38 mm, and the overall width at 81 mm; the organizer in the viewer has taller drawers, the original drawers see-through behind them

steps.title: Make the drawers fit business cards
text: For a change with a purpose, tell SOMA AI the measurements of what must fit, and ask it to show a card in each drawer. It works out how big the drawers have to be inside, makes the body just wide enough, builds it and checks that the drawers still slide out. In the video this took 5 min 21 s.
The organizer is now 96 mm wide. Each drawer has 89 by 59 mm inside, 2 mm of room around a card, and the height stays the same.

To look inside, use the Section tool. It only cuts open the view, the model itself does not change. From above you see the green see-through card lying flat in the upper drawer, and the amber outline of the old drawer, far too small for it.
steps.prompt: I want to keep business cards (85 x 55 mm) lying flat in both drawers. Make the organizer just big enough that they fit, with a few millimeters of room, and keep the drawers sliding freely. Show one business card as a thin see-through block in each drawer, so I can see that it fits. Keep the original as reference.

image.alt: The wider organizer cut open with the Section tool on Z at 38 mm: a green see-through business card in the upper drawer and the amber outline of the old, smaller drawer; SOMA AI's reply says 96 x 128 x 95 mm and 89 x 59 mm of floor space per drawer

steps.title: Sketch a third drawer with Mark up
text: Instead of describing where something goes, draw it. Click Mark up above the viewer and sketch on a side view: a rectangle under the drawers, an arrow from the front to the back and a few words. Then click Send to agent and add one sentence: the pen cup should stay just as deep.
SOMA AI adds a drawer underneath, as deep as the whole organizer, and lifts the pen cup with everything above it, so the cup stays just as deep. In the video this took 6 min 25 s.

Now there are three drawers. The new drawer is 25 mm high, the organizer is now 124.5 mm tall instead of 95 mm, and the cards still fit in the two upper drawers. A cut through the side shows it best: the new drawer runs all the way to the back, under the pen cup, and the cup is still 90 mm deep.
steps.prompt: Add a third drawer here, like in my sketch: under the other two, all the way to the back. The pen cup should stay just as deep as it is now.

image.alt: Mark up on a side view of the organizer: an orange rectangle under it with an arrow from the front to the back and the words 3rd drawer, all the way back, with the Send to agent button below

steps.title: Check the new drawer with a section
text: Use the Section tool on X to cut the organizer from the side. You see the two upper drawers with their cards, the new bottom drawer reaching the back wall under the pen cup, and the cup itself, still as deep as before.

image.alt: The organizer cut open on X at 5 mm: two upper drawers with green cards and a new bottom drawer that runs to the back under the pen cup; SOMA AI's reply says the pen cup remains 90 mm deep and the overall height is now 124.5 mm

steps.title: Compare it with the original
text: Ask SOMA AI to put the original next to the new organizer. It moves the original over, with a gap and the fronts lined up. In the video this took 2 min 18 s.
Side by side: the download on the left, your version on the right. Wider, a bit taller, with room for business cards and a third drawer that goes all the way back.
steps.prompt: Move the original reference to the left of the new organizer, with a gap, so I can compare them side by side.

image.alt: The original organizer in see-through amber on the left and the new blue organizer on the right, wider and taller, with three drawers

steps.title: Export it for your slicer
text: Click Export at the top and choose 3MF or STL for your slicer. With All parts, each part becomes its own file: the body and all three drawers, ready to print. Reference parts such as the original are not included.
If you share your remix, credit the original author and keep the same license.

tips: Ask for the original as a see-through reference in the same place. It is the easiest way to check that the rebuild matches the download.
Give the real measurements of what must fit, and ask SOMA AI to show it in the model, like the see-through business cards in the video. Then check it with the Section tool.
Small size changes are quicker with the Parameters tab: no AI, no waiting, and Reset all goes back.
Say what must not change, like the depth of the pen cup. SOMA AI then keeps it and changes the rest around it.
Every change is saved in the History at the bottom, so you can always look at or restore an earlier version.

faq.q: Can you edit an STL file?
faq.a: Only in a limited way. An STL is a mesh of flat triangles, without sizes such as a width or a wall thickness, so you can move triangles but not simply make a part wider. To really change it, rebuild it as a model with real sizes. In SOMA, SOMA AI does that rebuild for you from the STL or 3MF.

faq.q: Does this work with 3MF files too?
faq.a: Yes. The video uses a 3MF, the format slicers use, and an STL works just the same. Both only store triangles, so SOMA shows them as a mesh and SOMA AI rebuilds the part as a real model.

faq.q: What is the difference between an STL and a parametric model?
faq.a: An STL only stores the surface as triangles. A parametric model is built from sizes and rules, such as a width, a drawer height or a clearance, so changing one value rebuilds the whole part correctly. In SOMA those values show up as sliders in the Parameters tab.

faq.q: Can I convert an STL to STEP?
faq.a: Converting the triangles directly gives you a STEP file that is still just a mesh. Once SOMA AI has rebuilt the part as a real solid model in SOMA, Export writes a proper STEP file for other CAD programs, as well as STL and 3MF for printing.

faq.q: Am I allowed to change an STL I downloaded?
faq.a: That depends on its license, which you find on the model's page. The desk organizer in the video is under CC BY-SA 4.0: you may change it, but if you share your version you must credit the author, say what you changed and use the same license.

faq.q: Do I need CAD skills to change a downloaded part?
faq.a: No. You describe the change in plain words, give the measurements, sketch on the model with Mark up or drag a slider. SOMA AI rebuilds the part and SOMA shows the result, which you check against the original.
